tasks.notes: Canonical Composition projection is implemented and tested. Follow-up timeline patch also addresses the immediate #54 cross-model occupancy defect: ordinary clip drop/resize now considers Master Shots, resize trims update both Shots and Timeline Clips in one history transaction, and Master Shot drag identity survives protected dragover. This is an interim compatibility fix, not the final shared editor engine. Import/export migration and full root/nested editor unification remain outstanding. See docs/PROJECT_ROADMAP.md. The shared project-level placement/resize adapter is now extracted from App into `src/projectTimelinePlacement.ts`; it is the compatibility seam for the later canonical Composition editor. Schema-1.0 persistence/import/export are still unchanged. The compatibility engine now centralizes project-level placement move, drop calculation and resize preview/application in `src/projectTimelinePlacement.ts`; Master and ordinary clip move commits both use `moveProjectTimelinePlacement()`. Canonical schema persistence/import/export remains the next integration boundary. The canonical projection now represents each Master Shot as a root Composition placement and preserves every legacy Shot Slot Version as a separate legacy composition projection. Materialized `storyboard-*` placements are deduplicated against Master Shots; linked audio targets are remapped to the canonical Shot placement when necessary. Nested Clip Versions now receive additive `tracks[]` and `layers[].trackId` fields during load/import normalization. Legacy versions get deterministic Video/Audio/Text tracks while retaining layer kinds and source fields; existing valid track IDs/order are preserved. The migration projection now reuses these persisted track IDs. This is a backward-compatible schema-1.0 bridge, not the final schema-2.0 persistence format. Nested track normalization also retains pre-normalization effects/procedural lane kinds in `originalKind`, so the canonical projection does not erase that legacy information. Nested Clip Versions now use explicit track rows in the timeline UI, with multiple placements per track and track-aware add/move operations. This is still an additive schema-1.0 bridge, not the final persisted Composition schema. The nested editor now displays canonical Video/Audio/Text track rows with multiple placements per track, adds tracks separately from content placements, and supports compatible track-to-track placement moves. Exact-head CI run 39217800522 passed; the persisted project schema remains 1.0. The first versioned import/export boundary is integrated. New exports contain a canonical Composition projection alongside the legacy project payload; imports accept old schema-1.0 files and the new envelope without loss. The editor still runs on the legacy payload, so schema-2.0 is not yet authoritative persistence. Latest code CI run 39218695102 passed tests, TypeScript and Vite build. The versioned document reader now rejects schema-2.0 envelopes whose project ID/name or root Composition ID conflicts with the embedded schema-1.0 project; regression tests cover mismatched project identity and root identity. Exact-head CI run 39221701720 passed tests and TypeScript/Vite build at 3826f84cd529ad2461a07f26ab83adf7a5a5b526. This is an envelope integrity guard only; it does not make the projection authoritative or implement structure-preserving Save-as-Clip. Latest slice: readProjectDocument now recomputes the canonical migration projection and rejects stale/tampered root placements, nested Clip compositions, Shot Slot compositions, or migration warnings instead of silently loading an inconsistent envelope. Regression tests cover tampered placements and a fresh versioned round-trip. Pending exact-head CI; this remains a transitional guard, not canonical schema-2 persistence or structure-preserving Save-as-Clip. Latest interaction slice adds a tested nested timeline adapter over the shared placement/resize calculation contract, including snap/drop previews, overlap prevention and atomic adjacent-layer trims. This improves #53/#54 behavior but does not promote schema-2 Composition to authoritative persistence; canonical editor state and structure-preserving Save-as-Clip remain planned. PR #63 was merged and deployed as `9da2f2bfbf7e80abb73f5552a0d1447cff471c0b`; main CI 39227655141 and Pages deployment 39227655137 succeeded. This improves the nested editor interaction slice but does not make schema-2 Composition authoritative or finish structure-preserving Save-as-Clip; keep DYS-014 in progress. Product clarification requested by owner (2026-10-19): current Storyboard add creates a Shot Slot plus empty Slot Version, not a separate reusable Asset Clip. Existing Clip Assets can duplicate an existing version; PR #66 shipped a New Blank Version command for reusable Clip Assets (functional code SHA `ee1f90c3304ce0f2be5cef294c387192d2aa8969`; CI 39234313896 and Pages 39234313840 passed). This does not unify Shot Slot Versions with reusable Clip Asset Versions or finish structure-preserving Save-as-Clip. Keep Shot Slot Version vs reusable Clip Asset Version as distinct legacy entities for now; the unified Composition relationship and structure-preserving snapshots remain unfinished. Do not auto-create duplicate linked Asset Clips for every Shot until this is an explicit product decision. Current published main checkpoint for safe Add Clip insertion is `990158fc70cf0e6fe17a994237c1b0d65b7d60fb`, with CI 39233639480 and Pages deploy 39233639536 passed. Shot/Slot Version vs reusable Clip Asset Version remains separate legacy persistence; don't auto-create linked duplicate Asset Clips for every new Shot without an explicit owner decision.
